author: Karl Rock
description:
Begging scams can be confronting, especially when someone appears to have a serious injury.

For most of us, the first time we saw the idea of beggars being deliberately disfigured was in Slumdog Millionaire. Seeing something that reminded me of that while travelling through Pakistan was shocking.

If you're travelling in Pakistan, don't feel pressured into giving money just because someone approaches you or shows you an injury. Keep your distance, stay calm, and don't get drawn into an argument.

If you genuinely want to help, consider donating through a reputable local charity instead. That way, your money can support people who need it without rewarding aggressive or potentially exploitative begging.

title: The Most Disturbing Scam I’ve Seen

author: Karl Rock
description:
Indian food is available in Pakistan, despite the complicated relationship between the two countries. So while travelling in Karachi, I decided to put it to the test.

I headed to Mirchili Restaurant in Karachi, a Pakistani chain with branches around the city serving chaat and, at some locations, dosa. At this particular branch inside a shopping mall, I tried two classic Indian snacks: Bhel Puri and Raj Kachori, which Mirchili calls Khas Gappa Ghotala on its menu.

Having travelled all around India and eaten food in every Indian state, I have a pretty good idea of what these dishes are supposed to taste like. So how does Indian food made in Pakistan compare with the real thing in India?

The Bhel Puri was… interesting. The presentation was very different from what I'm used to in India, and it was loaded with chilli. But despite how it looked, it actually tasted much better than I expected.
